schema.description:
What a caller sends: a JSON-RPC envelope. Not the whole of the protocol —
three methods answered, which are the ones this serves — but the envelope
itself is every client's, so it is accepted whole rather than trimmed to
what today's handler happens to read. No `deny_unknown_fields`: a field a
future protocol version adds is not this caller's mistake.

No `id` means no answer is wanted — a JSON-RPC notification. A real client
never sends `id: null` for a request it wants answered, so that is read the
same way as an absent one rather than kept apart with a second `Option`.

When the page it is about was written. What a listing is ordered and

Key.description: One key this site has out. Not the key itself: that was shown once.

id.description: Enough of the hash to tell two keys apart, and not enough to be one.

posts.description:
How much is written in it. What somebody wants to know before taking one
away, and the reason taking one away is refused.

Learner.description: Whoever is watching, as their own screen shows them.

redirect.description:
Where in the panel to land afterwards, and where the provider sends
them back to.

video_id.description: What a student watches, where a lesson has one.

done.description:
Whether this student has finished it. Always false when a panel is
asking: it is a fact about a person, and nobody is one here.

Letter.description:
One letter as a screen sees it: what it says, and whether that is the site's
own wording or this machine's.

theirs.description:
False where this is what the machine says because the site has not said
anything.

Mail.description: What was sent, and what became of it.

site.description: What the site is called, for the tab and the header.

site_state.description: `active`, or `on_hold` for a site that may be read and not written.

Money.description:
An amount in minor units. There is no conversion from a float, in either
direction, so a price cannot arrive through one.

stages.description:
The columns it starts with. A board with no stages is a board nothing
can be put on, so there is a default rather than an empty one.

code.description:
Typed by a customer, so it is kept as one case and compared as one:
upper, which is what the database already insists on.

value.description: A percentage, or an amount in the smallest unit. The kind says which.

secret.description:
Sealed on the way in and never handed back. Nothing in this API returns
one, which is why there is no endpoint that reads them.

trigger.description:
The event that starts it. Checked against what this build can emit, so
a flow waiting for something nothing sends is refused rather than
quietly never running.

code.description:
`en`, or `en-GB`. What the database already insists on, said here as
well so that the refusal is a sentence rather than a constraint name.

is_default.description:
Whether this becomes the one a post is written in when nobody said. The
first language a site adds is, whatever it says.

position.description: Where it sits. Left out, it goes last.

type.description:
A site's own kind of thing, by name. What it declares is what may be
written in `fields`.

translation_of.description: Writing this as another language's version of something already here.

price_minor.description:
In minor units. There is no way to send a price as a decimal, which is
how a price comes to be 19.989999999.

oneOf.description: What several of them are called, where that is a different word.

names.description:
What it is called in each language a site writes in, as
`{"tr": {"name": "Kitap", "plural": "Kitaplar"}}`. Left out, what is
already written down stays.

key.description:
Only where one is being made. Changing a type's name would change what
every post of it is, so this is not a thing that can be edited.

media_id.description:
The file it is made from, already uploaded. A video that is not a file
on this machine is not something this can hand to anybody.

Offered.description: What a sign-in screen needs to draw a button, and nothing else.

OnCourse.description:
Somebody on a course. Not [`Enrolled`], which carries the token that put
them there and is shown once.

number.description:
What a customer calls it, counted per site. Nobody writes to a shop
about a uuid.

Overview.description:
What a site adds up to.

One question rather than a screen making eleven: the first thing anybody
opens is this, and eleven requests is eleven chances to draw half of it.

written.description: Day by day over the window asked for, oldest first.

PageRead.description: One page, and how much it was read.

oneOf.description:
Somebody's address, changed. What was proved about the old one is not
proved about this one, so it goes back to unproved and a link is sent —
an address typed by somebody else is how an account gets taken over.

Placed.description:
What comes back from checking out: the order, and where to go and pay for
it. A site with no provider configured has the first and not the second.

Plugged.description:
One integration, as a screen sees it. The secret half is not here and there
is no endpoint that answers with it.

settings.description: What was given, minus everything the plugin keeps.

holds.description: Which secrets are set, without saying what they are.

settings.description:
Everything the plugin wants, secrets included. What is not given again
is kept as it was, so a screen does not have to re-type a password to
change a port.

type.description: A site's own kind of thing, by name, where it is one.

cover_media_id.description: The picture that goes with it, where a site has chosen one.

seo_title.description:
What a search engine and a chat app show. Both fall back to the title
and the excerpt, which is what a site that says nothing here wants.

canonical.description: Where this was published first, when that was somewhere else.

translation_of.description:
The post this is a translation of, where it is one. What links a group
together; which of them is the original means nothing beyond being
written first.

publish_at.description:
When a scheduled post should go. Required to schedule one, ignored
otherwise.

log.description:
What the build said, where it said anything. Read on the one day it
matters: a build that failed and nothing saying why is a person
guessing at somebody else's compiler.

left_alone.description: What was already here under the same address and was left alone.

codes.description: Shown once, here, and never again: what is stored is their hashes.

environment.description: What was gathered rather than asked for.

media_id.description: A picture, where one was sent.

Request.description:
What a caller sends: a JSON-RPC envelope. Not the whole of the protocol —
three methods answered, which are the ones this serves — but the envelope
itself is every client's, so it is accepted whole rather than trimmed to
what today's handler happens to read. No `deny_unknown_fields`: a field a
future protocol version adds is not this caller's mistake.

No `id` means no answer is wanted — a JSON-RPC notification. A real client
never sends `id: null` for a request it wants answered, so that is read the
same way as an absent one rather than kept apart with a second `Option`.

second_factor.description: The six digits, where the account it turns out to be asks for them.

grants.description:
The whole set, not a change to it: a role is what it may reach, and
sending only what is added leaves nobody able to take one away.

kind.description: `broken`, `missing` or `wanted`. What decides who looks at it and when.

environment.description:
Gathered rather than asked for: the browser, the window, and whatever
had already gone wrong on the screen.

media_id.description:
A picture, as a file this site already holds. Uploaded first, so that
what is stored is a file rather than a megabyte of base64 in a column.

screen.description: What they were looking at, as they were looking at it.

p75.description:
The seventy-fifth: what three in four people got or better, which is
what these are judged by everywhere else.

verdict.description:
`good`, `could_be_better` or `poor`, by the thresholds published for
each measurement rather than by anything decided here.

Seen.description:
The one endpoint here a visitor reaches. Everything it is given is bounded
before it is stored, and the form is found by the name on the address rather
than by an id the caller supplies.
How many were waiting.

state.description: What comes back with the answer, so the panel can hand it over again.

Settings.description:
What a site's own people may see of its settings.

`contact` and `notes` are the operator's, not the site's, and are not here:
they are how one machine's operator keeps track of who to talk to, which is
nothing to do with whoever runs the site.

storage_used_bytes.description:
How much has been uploaded, and how much may be. Read here rather than
set: what a site is allowed is the operator's to decide, and finding out
at the point of an upload being refused is finding out too late.

Slow.description:
One page, at the seventy-fifth of each measurement.

All four rather than the one it is ordered by: somebody looking at the
slowest page wants to know which part of it is slow, and a second request
per page to find out is a screen that makes twenty requests.

Slug.description: A Slug, parsed on the way in rather than checked later.

recovery_codes_left.description:
Null where it is not enabled. Zero here is somebody one lost phone away
from being locked out, and the panel says so.

last_seen_at.description: When they were last actually here. Null is never.

courses.description: How many courses they are on. What somebody looks at before suspending.

suspended.description: Stopping somebody, or letting them back in.

pages.description:
The pages people actually read, most read first. Where a site finds out
that the page it worked on is not the one anybody opens.

Taken.description: What one step of a run did, and what it said if it failed.

TermChanges.description:
What may be changed about one. The kind and the language are not here: a
category that becomes a tag is a different thing under the same posts, and
making one is how a site says that.

parent_id.description:
The nil uuid means "under nothing", because a missing field means
"leave it alone" and both have to be sayable.

TermKind.description:
A category nests and a tag does not, and that is the whole of the
difference. Two tables is how the two came to disagree about a post.

goes_at.description: When it stops being restorable and goes for good.

Title.description: A Title, parsed on the way in rather than checked later.

unseen.description: What has come in through a form and nobody has read.

Translation.description: The same writing, in another language.

TypeField.description: One field a kind of thing carries.

name.description:
What the field is called in the data: the key a post's `fields` holds
it under, and what a theme reads.

label.description:
What a person sees above the box. The name, where nothing else is said
— which is what a site whose fields are already words wants.

choices.description: For a field that is one of a few things. Empty for the rest.

plays.description:
Where it plays, and in what sizes. Whatever transcoded it decides the
shape of this; nothing here reads into it.

Vitals.description: How the site felt to whoever was on it.

worst.description:
The pages doing worst on the one that matters most for the feeling of a
page loading. A screen that says a site is slow and not which page is a
screen nobody can act on.

needed.description:
Whether this machine still has nobody to run it. False for ever after
the first account, and nothing here says anything else about it.

Watching.description: One lesson, as somebody on the course reads it.

body.description:
What the lesson says. Kept when access ends: it is the video that
stops, not the notes.

position.description: Which of how many, over the whole course.

video_id.description: What to play, where there is one and this person may watch it.

order.description:
Nested rather than flattened: a flattened struct has no shape a
generated client can name, and the panel's types come from this.

lines.description:
Called lines rather than items: `items` is what a page of something
holds, everywhere else in this API, and one order is not a page.

WholeFlow.description: A flow and the steps in it, in order.

WholePost.description:
One post, and what else it is: the terms it is filed under and the same
writing in other languages.

Together rather than as three requests: an editor opening a post needs all
of it, and three round trips is three chances to draw half a screen.

WholeRun.description: A run and every step it took.
